source_title: Performance evaluation of an emergency department in Rio de Janeiro: a hybrid approach using Discrete Events Simulation and Data Envelopment Analysis
locator: Table 6 (empirical means); Table 7 (T1 model input); Appendix 2 (T1 fit expression and diagnostics).
source_setting: One private hospital emergency department in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; nurse triage, daytime shift T1.
source_period: Records span 2022-02-01 to 2023-09-30, excluding August 2023; fitting window not specified.
source_n: 130,525 total attendances over 19 months; triage duration missing 55.07%; fitting sample n not reported.
quantity: T1 triage time: empirical mean versus two printed shifted-lognormal model inputs
parameterization: Expressions copied as printed. ARENA guide defines LOGN parameters as mean and standard deviation of the unshifted lognormal variate; adding 1.5 implies means of 3.36 and 2.55 minutes, respectively. These derived means are arithmetic implications, not values reported by the article.
fit_method: Article says Input Analyzer selected fits; Table 7 and Appendix 2 disagree on T1 expression. The exact fitting subset and handling of missingness are not reported.
source_evidence_basis: Inspected publisher-hosted full-text PDF. Table 6 reports T1 triage mean 3.81 minutes (95% CI 3.76-3.85); Table 7 prints 1.5 + LOGN(1.86, 1.32), whereas Appendix 2 prints 1.5 + LOGN(1.05, 0.848).
limitations: The paper gives no erratum located in the publisher/SciELO search. Triage time is 55.07% missing and the fit sample count/window are absent. Neither printed expression can be selected from the article alone; implied means differ from the reported empirical mean.
inferred_scenario_use: Retain both expressions as conflicting source reports for audit only; do not choose either as a calibrated distribution or transfer it to RWJ.
conflict_resolution: unresolved_source_conflict; convention clarified, fitted input not validated

source_title: Performance evaluation of an emergency department in Rio de Janeiro: a hybrid approach using Discrete Events Simulation and Data Envelopment Analysis
locator: Methods, verification/validation description; Results, Table 8 discussion; Appendix 2, distribution-fit statistics; Appendix 6, observed-versus-simulated Mann-Whitney results.
source_setting: One private hospital emergency department in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; triage and consultation service-time inputs.
source_period: Records span 2022-02-01 to 2023-09-30, excluding August 2023; fit sample period not specified.
source_n: 130,525 total attendances; triage duration missing 55.07%, consultation duration missing 16.46%; stage fit n not reported.
quantity: Fit goodness-of-fit statistics and model validation evidence

value.appendix_2_fit_tests: All four process/shift rows show test values and parenthetical (<0.05) for Kolmogorov-Smirnov and chi-square columns.
value.observed_vs_simulated_comparison: Body says observed and simulated stage/total means differed significantly; Appendix 6 reports p<0.05 for all listed comparisons.

unit: test statistics and reported p-value thresholds
source_evidence_basis: Publisher PDF inspected. The appendix presents numerical fit-test statistics with parenthetical <0.05 annotations; these are not clearly labeled p-values in the table structure. Separately, the article describes validation against observed process lengths of stay and reports significant differences (p<0.05).
limitations: No inspected body statement saying fit-test p-values exceed 0.05 was located; the Appendix 2 formatting itself leaves the interpretation of the parentheses and values unclear. Validation comparisons concern process lengths of stay, not proof that fitted input distributions fit. No public correction/supplement was found in targeted journal/SciELO search.
inferred_scenario_use: Do not claim the input distributions passed goodness-of-fit or that the simulation was validated to observed stage timing. Separate input fit diagnostics from downstream model validation.

locator: Appendix A, printed pages 116, 117 and 119 (PDF pages 124,125,127)
source_setting: Rockwell Automation Arena simulation software documentation; not a hospital study.
source_period: Guide edition hosted by Aarhus University; the guide is older than the 2024 Rio study.
quantity: Arena LOGN, GAMM and EXPO argument conventions

value.parameter_meaning: Mean and standard deviation of the lognormal random variable X
value.not_parameter_meaning: The guide separately denotes mean and SD of ln(X) as μ and σ; these are not the user-entered LogMean and LogStd.
value.gamma_syntax: GAMM(Beta, Alpha): scale first, shape second

unit: Parameter units follow the modeled quantity; Rio paper labels minutes.
source_evidence_basis: Rockwell-authored manual defines LOGN using arithmetic mean/SD of the lognormal draw, GAMM using scale then shape, and EXPO using mean. These conventions do not establish a valid fitted model.
limitations: Older Arena guide, hosted by a university mirror rather than current Rockwell documentation. It clarifies software convention only; it cannot resolve which Rio expression was intended or establish fit quality.
inferred_scenario_use: Use solely to interpret Arena notation: under this convention, each reported pair describes arithmetic mean and SD of the unshifted lognormal draw before the stated additive shift. Do not treat that interpretation as confirmation that the Rio fit is valid.

source_title: Improving Emergency Department radiology transportation time: a successful implementation of lean methodology
locator: Methods, Theoretical model and outcome measure (pp. 2-3); Results, Table 2 (p. 6); Discussion (p. 6).
source_setting: Emergency department, American University of Beirut Medical Center; plain radiography patients.
source_period: Pre-intervention 2012-10-17 to 2013-04-17; post-intervention 2013-05-19 to 2013-11-19, after one-month washout.
source_n: 6,186 pre-intervention radiographs; 4,879 post-intervention radiographs. Excludes 00:00-08:00 radiographs and patients leaving against medical advice or transferred.
quantity: Cashier order-processing to radiographer study-initiation transportation turnaround time
source_evidence_basis: Inspected publisher full text and university repository PDF. Methods explicitly define transportation TAT as cashier processing to PACS-recorded radiographer study initiation. Discussion later calls this the order-processing-to-study-completion step, while Methods distinguish initiation-to-completion as a separate interval.
limitations: Single center, retrospective nonrandomized pre/post operational study; exclusions and concurrent ED changes constrain transfer. The discussion endpoint wording conflicts with the operational definition in Methods.
inferred_scenario_use: Use as external reference for cashier-processed order to imaging-study initiation elapsed time, following the explicit Methods definition; do not relabel it as image completion or reporting time, and do not transfer as RWJ measurement.
conflict_resolution: interpretable_convention: Methods endpoint retained; conflicting Discussion shorthand preserved as limitation
